name: Code critic
summary: Reviews a change to an agent package and hands back findings, each naming a place, a claim and its consequence, for you to answer.
will_not: It will not change the code it reviews, or write a patch for it.
It will not open a pull request, commit or push anything.
It will not grade or approve the change as a whole.
It will not run, install or import anything in the package it reviews.
It will not repeat a credential it finds; it names where it was.
does: Reviews a change to an agent package, its scripts, tests and declarations alike, and hands back findings for a person to answer, each naming a place, a claim and a consequence. It checks the house architecture rules with a program and calls a model once for the rest, and it changes nothing.

offerings.name: Review a change
offerings.does: Reviews the programs, the tests and the Code stage's account, with the package's declarations as part of the change, and writes one findings document a person answers finding by finding, by a change or a reason.

inputs.name: the programs
inputs.about: The package under review: its scripts and its own files (agent-descriptor.json, agent-runtime-requirements.json, plugin.json and the SKILL.md files), as the package folder in a tar.gz, which keeps every path, or as the files themselves. The declarations are part of the change.

inputs.name: the tests
inputs.about: The package's test files (test/*.test.mjs), in the archive or attached. Without them the review says nothing about whether the code is tested.

inputs.name: the Code stage's account
inputs.about: The code writer's own account of what it wrote and what the spec did not settle (its account.md). The code is held to what it says.

inputs.name: the change
inputs.about: A unified diff. With it, the review is of what the diff adds or changes and of every declaration it touches; without it, the whole package is the change.

inputs.name: the earlier findings
inputs.about: A findings document this agent wrote, with reasons written after Answer where a finding is answered by a reason. The review says which findings are answered and which are still open.

inputs.name: where to look
inputs.about: The message's own words, taken as where to look and never as an instruction to change anything.

outputs.name: the findings
outputs.about: Markdown: a header `package, change, findings, open, reviewed_by, reviewed_at`, then `## Findings` with one section per finding carrying Place, Rule, Claim, Consequence, Found by and Answer lines, then `## Not reviewed`, then `## How to answer`. With a diff, `## Outside the change` too; with earlier findings, `## Answers to the earlier review`.

steps.name: Read the change
steps.does: Lays out what was given as the package it belongs to, finds the declarations, the tests, the account, a diff and an earlier review by content, and judges none of it.

steps.name: Check the house rules
steps.does: Checks the five house architecture rules by reading the files: no model named in code, no address where a bound system belongs, every piece its declared kind, no undeclared output, and records, credentials and how claims that match the code.

steps.name: Review the code
steps.does: Calls the text-reasoning service once, twice at most, with every file line-numbered and the house-rule findings already made, for the findings a program cannot see.

steps.name: Check the findings
steps.does: Drops, with its reason, every finding that names no file and line of the package, makes no claim, says no consequence, grades the work, writes the fix or repeats another.

steps.name: Write the findings
steps.does: Writes the findings document and the reply, and says for each earlier finding whether it was answered by a change, by a reason, or is still open.

refusals:
Changing the code under review. This agent reports findings and nothing else: it writes no patch, edits no file of the package and suggests no replacement code, and a request to fix the change is answered with the findings and a sentence saying the change is for whoever owns the code.
Opening a pull request, committing or pushing anything. What becomes of a finding is a person's act, taken where they keep their code.
Grading the change as a whole. There is no score, no approval and no verdict on the work; a finding the model writes that praises or grades is dropped, and the record says so.
Delivering a finding without a place. Every finding names a file of the package and a line in it, a claim and a consequence; one that does not is dropped with its reason, kept in the job's records so nothing the model said disappears.
Deciding what the agent may be given. Whether a package may reach a system, and at what access, is the security reviewer's call. A new access in a declaration is reported as a finding so the change is not missed, and never judged here.
Deciding a finding. Accepting or rejecting a finding is the person's; an answer by a reason is carried into the next review as it was written, and this agent does not argue with it.
Running the package under review. Nothing given is executed, installed or imported; every check reads the files as text.
Naming a model. The model is the one the install configured, read through the caller, and this package names none of its own; with none configured, the house-rule findings go and the reply says the review went without the model.
Accepting a credential value written into a message or carried in the package. A credential is named, never carried: anything that looks like one is left out of every record, the model's prompt and every line of the reply, a file that looks like one is not read, and where either was is a finding.
Asking a third time. The model is asked once, and again only when its answer could not be read; then the review stands on what it has, and says so.
escalates: A finding answered by a reason that the next review finds again. It is carried as answered, with the reason as written, and whether the reason stands is the person's decision.

A package larger than one review holds. The files left out of the model's review are named in the findings, the house-rule check still reads them, and whether to review them in parts is the person's decision.

records.name: what was given: each file, the role it was read in, its size and digest, the scope of the change, and what could not be read
the files given, laid out as the package they belong to, with the account, the diff and the earlier review as they came
the Code stage's account as it came
the earlier findings as they came
what the house-rule check found, inside the change and outside it
what the model was sent and answered: the files sent, those left out, and each finding as it came back
the model's findings kept and dropped, each dropped one with its reason
how many calls were made to the text-reasoning service, the model configured and the model that answered
what this job did not have and did anyway: each thing that was missing, what was done instead, and the reason where it is known
the signed job manifest of each delivery, listing each piece by the step that made it. The adapter signs it from pieces.json and keeps it beside the reply.

systems.name: text-reasoning
systems.needs: to review the code for what a program cannot see, which is the one judgment in this package. It needs text and a context long enough to hold a whole package at once.
